blocks.text: You can connect your Okta organization to Zscaler 3rd-Party App Governance to gain continuous visibility and governance for third-party apps installed in the Okta environment.
Okta integration consists of the following steps:

blocks.item: Creating a Dedicated Read-Only Service Account for 3rd-Party App Governance Integration
Getting the Okta API Token and Okta Domain
Connecting Okta to 3rd-Party App Governance

blocks.text: Ensure the following prerequisites are met:

blocks.item: A user with Okta Admin privileges
An Okta API token for an administrative account in your Okta organization

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends creating a dedicated service account for integration and assigning the minimum required privileges.

blocks.heading: Creating a Dedicated Read-Only Service Account for 3rd-Party App Governance Integration

blocks.text: To create a dedicated read-only service account:

blocks.item: Sign in to your Okta organization as a user with administrator privileges.
In the Okta Admin console, go to Directory > People, and then click Add person.
In the Add Person window, enter the information for the 3rd-Party App Governance service account, set the password, and then click Save.
In the Okta Admin console, go to Security > Administrators, and then click Add administrator.
Select the 3rd-Party App Governance service account, set the role to Super Administrator, and click Save.
Sign out and sign in to your Okta Admin console with the newly created 3rd-Party App Governance service account.

blocks.heading: Getting the Okta API Token and Okta Domain

blocks.text: To get your Okta API token and Okta domain:

blocks.item: Sign in to the Okta Admin console.

blocks.text: Zscaler recommends that you sign in with the dedicated service account that you created for 3rd-Party App Governance integration.

blocks.item: Create an API token in Okta.
Note the API token you created. You will need it in the following steps.

blocks.text: For security reasons, you cannot view the API key in plain text. You must store the API key securely.

blocks.item: From your Okta organization URL (e.g., yourdomain.okta.com), copy and save your Okta domain "yourdomain." Do not copy the entire Okta Admin console URL, or you can also just remove "-admin" from the URL.

blocks.text: To connect Okta to 3rd-Party App Governance:

blocks.item: Click Connect in the upper-right corner of the App Dashboard.

blocks.text: See image.

blocks.item: From the drop-down menu, select Okta.

blocks.text: See image.
The Add Integration window appears.

blocks.item: In the Add Integration window, enter the Okta URL and Token, and then click Connect.

blocks.text: See image.

You must select the SSPM Scan checkbox on the Add SaaS Application Tenant page in the Zscaler Admin Console to enable the SSPM scan feature for the tenant. To learn more, see Adding SaaS Application Tenants.

After a connection is achieved, it might take a while to pull and ingest all relevant application data depending on the size of your tenant. During this time, a message displays indicating that the integration is still being processed. After integration is completed, a success message appears, and the tenant details are updated on the Settings page. You then receive an email from Zscaler when the integration is ready for further review.
You can view the list of added tenants along with information such as integration status, enabled features, first connected time, last synced time, etc. on the Settings page.
You can update an Okta token that is currently in use. To update the Okta token:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.
In the Edit Integration window, click the Edit icon next to the API key.
Update the token and click the checkmark to save the changes.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.

blocks.item: Click Confirm if you want to override the connection.

blocks.text: The connection is updated.
You can edit an Okta connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To edit an Okta connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Edit icon next to the relevant integration.
In the Edit Integration window, edit the tenant details as required and click Save.

blocks.text: The connection is updated.
You can delete an Okta connection to 3rd-Party App Governance. To delete an Okta connection:

blocks.item: On the Settings page, click the Delete icon next to the relevant integration.

blocks.text: A confirmation window appears.

blocks.item: Click Confirm to continue.

blocks.text: The connection is deleted.
The following table lists the APIs used and the data collected after integration:

table: List of users and their profile attributes, such as name, email, status, and time of last login
User role assignments (e.g., admin, super admin, user, etc.)
List of user groups which are configured in the tenant (e.g., “All employees,” “Accounting,” etc.)
The list of users associated with each of the above groups
The list of apps associated with each of the above groups (e.g., “Salesforce” for the “Sales” group)
List of apps available in the tenant along with their metadata
List of users associated with each application
For some types of applications, a list of permission scopes granted to the application
List of API tokens that have been generated in the tenant, along with their metadata, such as token name, the user who generated it, and its creation and expiration dates
